name: Checkbox
summary: Lets people turn one option on or off, or pick any number of options from a list.
description: A checkbox is a binary choice with a visible label: checked or unchecked, and a third, partially checked look when it stands for a group whose members disagree. Several checkboxes side by side let people pick any number of options; one checkbox alone confirms a statement (accepting terms, remembering a session). A setting that takes effect immediately is a Switch; a choice of exactly one option is a Radio group.

anatomy.description: Root. Lays out the control, the label, the description and the message on a grid; carries the size and the forced state.
The box: the native checkbox, drawn by the component. Receives focus, holds the checked state and shows it with a mark (a check when checked, a bar when indeterminate).
Text naming the option. Provides the accessible name; activating it toggles the control.

The required mark of the Forms rule, at the end of the label after a word space: "(optional)" on a checkbox that is not required when the form marks optional checkboxs, "(required)" on a required checkbox when it marks required checkboxs (markedFields), nothing otherwise. The label's size, regular, the description's color (Forms decision forms-mark-style). On the web "(required)" is hidden from assistive technology, the required attribute saying it, and "(optional)" is part of the name.

On Android and Windows only, in place of the mark: an asterisk at the end of the label of a required checkbox, 4 px after it (2 px in small), at the label's size and weight (label.typography), in the error message's red (Forms decision forms-asterisk-style), kept in the accessible name. Never drawn on the web, iOS and macOS, so neither the reference rendering nor the Figma component draws it.
Optional help text under the label, associated with the control as its description.
Text saying what is wrong and what to do, under the description (or the label), aligned with the label, associated with the control as a description after the description. Shown only with a severity.

Glyph of the icon font saying the severity, named after it ("Error"): error, the Alert's glyph. At the start of the message, before its text, when severityIcon is message (or after-control, which a choice control draws in the message); never after the box, where the label or the options follow it.

properties.name: Size
properties.description: Box size, label and description text size scale together.

properties.name: Label
properties.description: What checking the box means, stated positively (Send me a weekly summary), without trailing punctuation.

properties.name: Description
properties.description: Help text: what happens when the box is checked, when it is not obvious from the label.

properties.name: Marked fields
properties.description: Which fields carry the required mark. A rule of the form, not of the field: a form sets it once, to the same value, for all its controls (Forms decision forms-marked-fields); the field draws its mark from its own required.

options.description: "(optional)" on the checkbox when it is not required, nothing when it is (default). The form says once, before its first field, "All fields are required unless marked optional.".
"(required)" on the checkbox when it is required, nothing when it is not: for a form where most fields are optional.
No mark: a checkbox outside a form, such as a table's filter or a setting applied at once.

properties.name: Required
properties.description: The box must be checked to submit the form (accepting terms). It draws the mark that markedFields asks for ("(required)" on a required checkbox, "(optional)" on one that is not), and the asterisk on Android and Windows.

properties.name: Message
properties.description: What is wrong and what to do, shown with a severity.

properties.name: Severity icon
properties.description: Where the severity icon goes, a rule of the form set once for all its controls (Forms decision forms-severity-icon-placement). A choice control offers message and none: its label or options follow the box, so a form set to after-control shows its icon in the message.

options.description: At the start of the message, before its text, 16 px (default; also what after-control draws here).

No icon: the message's own words say the severity (the fix of an error, what to check, what was confirmed). The component writes no severity word; a project whose messages do not say it starts them with the word and its language's colon ("Error: …").

properties.name: Severity
properties.description: What the check of the value found. A choice has nothing to confirm or to warn about, so only error exists (decision forms-severity).

options.description: Validation failed: the box takes the error border, the message says what to do and the control is exposed as in error (aria-invalid on the web).

properties.name: Disabled
properties.description: Prevents changing the value; the current value stays visible. Prefer keeping the option enabled and explaining why it cannot change.

states.description: Resting, unchecked: an outlined empty box.
Pointer over the box or its label. The empty box takes a light tint; a checked box does not change. Needs a pointing device: touch has no hover.
Keyboard focus on the box. Shows the shared focus ring outside the box; pointer focus shows none.
The option is on: the box fills with the brand color and shows a check mark.

Partially checked: the box stands for a group of options of which some are on. Set by the application through the platform's API (there is no attribute for it on the web); the box fills and shows a bar instead of a check. Toggling it checks or unchecks the whole group.
Severity error: the box border takes the error color and, while the box is unchecked, the subtle error fill (a checked or indeterminate box keeps its brand fill); the message says the error in text.
Non-interactive. Box, label and description drop to the shared disabled colors, checked or not; hover and focus do not apply.

notes: The box sits before the label, centered on the label's first line; the description sits under the label, aligned with it, and the message under the description (or the label), aligned with it, container.gap (6 px) after it.
A list of checkboxes stacks them vertically; the layout owns the spacing between them.
The whole row (box and label) toggles the value: the label is part of the target.

name.text: Computed from the label, associated with the control as its label element on the web. The description and the message are exposed as the accessible description, not as part of the name.

keyboard.action: Moves focus to the box. A disabled checkbox is not focusable and is skipped.
Checks or unchecks the box. A partially checked box becomes checked.

guidelines.text: Expose the checkbox role, its name and its checked state through the platform's native checkbox control, so assistive technology receives them without extra work.
Use the native input type=checkbox: it exposes the checkbox role and its checked, mixed and disabled states without ARIA. Never add aria-checked to it.
Group related checkboxes under a visible group name, so people know what the set of options is about.

The partially checked state exists only through the platform's API: on the web it is the indeterminate IDL attribute, set by script, which the browser exposes as the mixed checked state. The reference implementation styles it; it cannot set it.
Never rely on color alone: the state is shown by the mark (check or bar), not only by the fill; an error is stated in text, not only by the red border.

Label, description and message contrast at least 4.5:1 with the surface in every color mode and enabled state: 19.03:1 and 12.78:1 in light mode, 11.28:1 and 8.86:1 in dark mode on the default surface; the error message 6.12:1 (light) and 7.06:1 (dark), at least 5.82:1 and 5.31:1 on every surface level. Disabled text is inactive and exempt.

The box is what identifies the control and shows its state, so its border, its fill and its mark contrast at least 3:1 with adjacent colors in every color mode: unchecked border 12.78:1 (light) and 11.28:1 (dark) on the default surface; checked fill 5.77:1 and 12.76:1; the mark on the fill 5.72:1 and 13.05:1. The focus ring 5.77:1 and 12.76:1. Disabled is exempt.
The error border (the accent functional border) contrasts 6.12:1 (light) and 4.97:1 (dark) with the default surface, and at least 5.79:1 and 3.73:1 on every surface level.
A visible focus indicator appears when the box receives keyboard focus, drawn outside the box.
The focus ring is drawn with :focus-visible, so pointer focus shows no ring.

The box alone is 16 or 20 CSS pixels, under the 24 pixel minimum; the label is part of the target and brings the row above it, and the spacing exception applies when a list leaves 24 pixels between rows.

When the value is in error, say so with aria-invalid on the input and say the error in the message, which aria-describedby references after the description. A checkbox has only the error severity: a choice has nothing to confirm or to warn about.
A required box uses the required attribute; the label or the description says that it must be checked.
The native disabled attribute removes the box from the focus order. When people need to know an option exists, keep it enabled and explain why it cannot change.
Apple recommends a hit region of at least 44 x 44 pt; the row (box and label) must reach it on iOS. Avoid relying solely on different colors to communicate the state.

Android recommends a touch target of at least 48 x 48 dp; Material's Checkbox sets that minimum itself when it can receive actions. Lift the toggle to the row with the toggleable modifier and the Checkbox role, so the label and the box form one element whose state is announced.
Color transitions of the box are removed when the user asks for reduced motion.

The severity icon is named after the severity ("Error") and is part of the description: at the start of the message it is inside the message, which aria-describedby references. It is never the only cue: the message says what is wrong. The icon reaches 3:1 on every surface level (at the lowest: error 5.81:1 (light) and 5.30:1 (dark)).
The mark comes after the label's words, so the visible label starts with the checkbox's name, and so does the accessible name when it ends with "(optional)": speech input by the label works.
On Android, the Checkbox draws the asterisk of a required checkbox in the error text color whenever markedFields is optional or required, none drawing no mark; an optional checkbox carries none.
On Windows, the asterisk stays in the Checkbox's UI Automation Name: the Name is the label as shown ("I accept the terms*").

guidelines: State the option positively, as what happens when the box is checked: Send me a weekly summary, never Do not send.
Sentence case, no trailing punctuation; one line when possible.
Put consequences and conditions in the description, not in the label.
A required checkbox (terms, consent) says what is agreed to in its label; the error message says what to do: Check the box to continue.

examples.description: A required consent left unchecked; the message says what to do.

props.label: I accept the terms of service

examples.name: Medium, in a form that marks required fields
examples.description: Most fields of the form are optional, so the form marks the required ones (markedFields required): "(required)" after the label, hidden from assistive technology, which the required state already tells.

decisions.text: The Checkbox draws the required mark of the Forms rule: the property markedFields (optional by default, required, none), set once per form to the same value for all its controls; the part mark at the end of its label after a word space, "(optional)" on a checkbox that is not required when the form marks optional fields, "(required)" on a required one when it marks required fields, nothing with none; the label's size, regular, in the description's color (checkbox.mark.*, its color aliasing form.mark.color.default); on the web "(required)" is hidden from assistive technology, the required state saying it, and "(optional)" is part of the name. The part asterisk, on Android and Windows only, ends the label of a required checkbox in the error text color (checkbox.asterisk.*, aliasing form.asterisk.color.default), 4 px after it (2 px in small), kept in the Windows UI Automation Name. The Figma component draws the web specification: a BOOLEAN Mark (on) and a TEXT Mark text, markedFields kept out of the variants (blueprint option fixed); the asterisk is not drawn.
decisions.rationale: Applies the Forms decisions forms-marked-fields, forms-mark-style, forms-asterisk-style, forms-required-windows-name (#103 step 16, #105 steps 4 and 2b, moved here by #105 step 12), as the field family's mark-part does. Built in #103 step 31.

decisions.text: The Checkbox gets the severity icon (part severity-icon) and the property severityIcon, as the Forms foundation decided for every form control that shows a severity: at the start of the message only: it offers message (default) and none, and draws a form's after-control in the message, its label or options following the box. Its size: 16 px (size.2), space.4 before the text. Its glyph is the Alert's, error, named "Error"; its color the on-base icon role of the severity, checkbox.severity-icon.color.* aliasing form.severity-icon.color.*. Drawn with the Text field's rules and Figma helpers.
decisions.rationale: Applies the Forms decisions forms-severity-icon-placement, forms-severity-icon-size, forms-severity-icon-color and forms-severity-icon-glyphs (#103 step 12 and #105 steps 6 and 12): the Select, the Checkbox and the groups take the field family's severity icon, built in #103 step 30.

decisions.text: The Checkbox has a message part (role errormessage), shown with a severity: under the description, or under the label without one, aligned with the label, container.gap (form.container.gap, 6 px) after what precedes it, in the Forms family's message color and sizes (message.color.error = form.message.color.error; message.typography small and medium at form.message.font-size.small and medium, 14 and 16 px, medium weight). The control's aria-describedby lists the description, then the message. It follows the Forms decisions forms-message-part-every-control ("every form control that can show a severity has a message part, after its description"), forms-part-gaps ("description → message", 6 px) and forms-text-sizes.
decisions.rationale: Applied in #105 step 12 (spec and docs fixes) from forms-message-part-every-control, decided by the team in #105 step 3 point 3 (A: the Checkbox gets its part with the complex controls). Measured then: the message reads 5.82 to 6.13:1 in light mode and 5.31 to 7.07:1 in dark mode on surface levels 0 to 3.

decisions.text: A checked or indeterminate box in error keeps its brand fill through a token for both states, control.background.checked-error and control.background.indeterminate-error (= global.bg.accent.brand.default, the role of the checked fill), inside its error border: a token path may name two states, joined by a hyphen in the spec's state order, and such a token applies when both hold and wins over the token of each state alone (packages/tokens/AGENTS.md, Which token applies). The path stays the only thing that says when a component token applies, so the token inspector, pnpm validate, the Specs export and the Figma and Penpot variants Severity=error, State=checked and State=indeterminate (4 variants) take the brand fill the web always drew; since error-fill they took control.background.error. No rendered value changes on the web.
decisions.rationale: Decided by the team on 2026-11-27 (#105 step 2b, point b3.1): "A", as recommended, a token for two states. Rejected: B, a precedence per slot declared in the spec's states (no token, but a reader of the tokens alone, such as Tokens Studio, the Style Dictionary outputs or a Specs reader without the sidecar, would still get the error fill); C, accept the inspector's simplification and give the Figma plan a hand-written rule. The state segment is one, checked-error, not two (checked.error): a DTCG token cannot also be a group, and checked already holds a value; the CSS variable is the same either way. Measured on the review sheet: the mark on the brand fill 5.72:1 in light mode and 13.06:1 in dark mode, on the error fill the Figma variants drew 1.11:1 and 1.01:1 (WCAG 1.4.11 asks 3:1).

decisions.text: The Checkbox's component tokens alias the Forms family (form.*) wherever their value is the family's default: the box's fill at rest, on hover and in error, its border in error, the label's color and font sizes, the description's color and its small font size. No value changes. Overrides, kept until this component's own refinement: the box's border at rest stays global.border.accent.neutral.default, where the family has the field family's global.border.base.neutral.5, and the medium description stays 14 px (body.size.sm), where the family has 12 px. Disabled colors, geometry and checked colors stay its own.
decisions.rationale: Follows the Forms foundation's decision forms-token-family (#105 step 2b, point b6, decided by the team on 2026-11-27): the default decisions for a form control rely on form.* tokens, which a control can override for specific use cases.

decisions.text: An unchecked box in error takes the subtle error fill (control.background.error = global.bg.subtle.functional.error.default) inside its error border, at rest and on hover alike; a checked or indeterminate box keeps its brand fill, so checked still reads checked. On hover an empty box in error keeps its fill and its error border (before, hover turned its border back to the neutral one).
decisions.rationale: Decided by the team on 2026-11-26 (#105 step 2b, point b3, option B chosen over the recommended A, border only); it follows the Forms foundation's decision forms-choice-error-fill, where the options and their reasons are recorded. Measured: The error border on the fill 5.45:1 in light mode and 5.14:1 in dark mode (WCAG 1.4.11 asks 3:1), on the surface levels 0 to 3 unchanged (6.12 / 5.79 / 6.12 / 5.79:1 light, 4.97 / 4.55 / 4.16 / 3.73:1 dark); the fill against the surface 1.12 / 1.06 / 1.12 / 1.06:1 light and 1.03 / 1.12 / 1.23 / 1.37:1 dark, decoration, not the cue.

decisions.text: The box shows the error severity, set by the severity property (none by default, error): its border takes the accent functional error border color. Warning and success do not exist for a single choice (our judgment, not a source's). Severity replaces the invalid property. On the web the error is aria-invalid="true" and data-severity on the root. The Checkbox still has no message part: the form says the error in text next to the box (Forms step 2b). The accent error border reaches 3:1 on every surface level since the Color foundation 7.1.0 (decision border-accent-functional-3-to-1).
decisions.rationale: The team validated the Forms foundation's three severities (decision forms-validation-severities) and named the property severity; "error" is the word every platform uses (WCAG 3.3.1 Error Identification, Compose error semantics, Material error text), where "invalid" is the web's technical term. The clean break is deliberate: the packages are alpha and unreleased, and a deprecated alias would cost a schema field and support in the validator, the bridge and the templates. This amends decisions field-colors and label-description-error, whose text still says invalid and error message.

decisions.text: The box is outlined in the accent neutral border color on the default surface when unchecked, and filled with the accent brand color with a mark in the on-accent brand icon color when checked or partially checked; hover tints the empty box with the surface hover color; an invalid box takes the base error border; disabled takes the shared disabled colors. The same colors hold for the Radio group and the Switch.
decisions.rationale: The Figma library maps no color to form controls. The accent neutral border is the lightest neutral border that keeps 3:1 against the surface in both modes (WCAG 1.4.11); the brand fill makes the on state the same as the brand action color.

decisions.text: A state is one token path segment: hover changes the empty box only; a checked, partially checked or disabled box does not change on hover.

Two sizes: small (16 px box, 14 px label) and medium (20 px box, 16 px label, the default), from the Figma library's size and body scales; the box border is 1.2 px (stroke-width.md) and its corners 2 px (small) or 4 px (medium).
A checkbox always has a visible label, which names it, and may have a description under the label, which is exposed as its accessible description.

changelog.note: Decision mark-part (#103 step 31; Forms forms-marked-fields, forms-mark-style, forms-asterisk-style, forms-required-windows-name): property markedFields (optional by default), parts mark and asterisk in the label, tokens checkbox.mark.* and checkbox.asterisk.* (colors aliasing form.mark.color.default and form.asterisk.color.default), the mark in the template ("(required)" aria-hidden) and the CSS, a web, an Android and a Windows guideline, the Figma Mark and Mark text with markedFields fixed. New example: Medium, in a form that marks required fields. The mark is 12.09:1 at the lowest in light mode and 6.65:1 in dark mode (forms-mark-style). A checkbox that is not required now shows "(optional)" by default; a control outside a form sets markedFields none (the docs site's controls and the dashboard and calendar screens do).

Decision severity-icon (#103 step 30; Forms forms-severity-icon-placement, -size, -color, -glyphs): part severity-icon and property severityIcon (message, none; message by default), tokens checkbox.severity-icon.* (font, size, gap, color aliasing form.severity-icon.color.*), the icon in the template (named after the severity, role img) and the CSS, a web guideline on its name; the Figma blueprint draws it with the Text field's helpers. An error now starts its message with the icon by default. Icon on the surface at the lowest: error 5.81:1 (light) and 5.30:1 (dark).

Decision message-part, after the Forms decisions forms-message-part-every-control, forms-part-gaps and forms-text-sizes (#105 step 12): a message part and a message property; the message sits under the description (or the label), aligned with the label, 6 px after it (container.gap = form.container.gap), in form.message.color.error at form.message.font-size.small and medium (14 and 16 px), medium weight; aria-describedby lists the description, then the message. The required-and-error example says its error in the message ("Check the box to continue"), not in the description. Message on the surfaces: 5.82 to 6.13:1 in light mode, 5.31 to 7.07:1 in dark mode (levels 0 to 3).

Decision checked-error-fill (#105 step 2b, point b3.1): a checked or indeterminate box in error keeps its brand fill through new tokens for two states, control.background.checked-error and control.background.indeterminate-error, which the CSS reads; the token inspector, pnpm validate, the Specs export and the Figma and Penpot variants now take it too. No rendered value changes.

Decision form-family-aliases, after the Forms decision forms-token-family (#105 step 2b, point b6): the box's fill at rest, on hover and in error, its border in error, the label's color and font sizes, the description's color and its small font size alias the Forms family (form.*), every resolved value unchanged; the box's border at rest stays global.border.accent.neutral.default, where the family has the field family's global.border.base.neutral.5, and the medium description stays 14 px (body.size.sm), where the family has 12 px.

Forms decision forms-guidelines-once (#105 step 2b, point b5): the form-wide guidelines leave this specification, said once in the Forms foundation and listed on this page under "From the Forms foundation", by the tiers this control follows: the visible label and its association on the web (label element, aria-describedby). The references only they cited are dropped. No rendering change.

Decision error-fill (Forms forms-choice-error-fill, #105 step 2b, point b3): new token control.background.error → global.bg.subtle.functional.error.default, an unchecked box in error filled with it inside its error border, a checked or indeterminate box keeps its brand fill. The error border on the fill 5.45:1 in light mode and 5.14:1 in dark mode (WCAG 1.4.11 asks 3:1), on the surface levels 0 to 3 unchanged (6.12 / 5.79 / 6.12 / 5.79:1 light, 4.97 / 4.55 / 4.16 / 3.73:1 dark); the fill against the surface 1.12 / 1.06 / 1.12 / 1.06:1 light and 1.03 / 1.12 / 1.23 / 1.37:1 dark, decoration, not the cue. On hover an empty box in error keeps its fill and its error border (before, hover turned its border back to the neutral one).
Fix: the examples' message and description of one sentence end with no period, as the Forms foundation decides (forms-message-punctuation). No rendering change.

Breaking, decision forms-severity: the invalid property is replaced by severity (none, error), errorMessage by message (the Checkbox has no message part), the state invalid by error; the web attribute data-invalid by data-severity. Tokens: control.border-color.invalid is control.border-color.error and reads the accent functional border (global.border.accent.functional.<severity>.default) instead of the base error border. CSS: [data-severity="<severity>"] and [data-state="<severity>"]. The accent error border reaches 3:1 on every surface level since the Color foundation 7.1.0 (decision border-accent-functional-3-to-1).

Fix, no decision changed: the Figma library's POC2 export (Color foundation 3.1.0) moves the values of the roles the tokens alias; the tokens, CSS and template are unchanged. Light: 7 tokens follow the ash retune (one to four units per channel). Dark: 5 tokens follow the ash retune (one to four units per channel); control.border-color.default, control.border-color.hover reads global.border.accent.neutral.default: #B9B7B7 becomes #CFCFCF; control.border-color.invalid reads global.border.base.functional.error.default: #E12A23 becomes #DF2821. Contrast re-measured on the accessibility guidelines: 3.82 → 3.73:1, 5.74 → 5.72:1, 5.79 → 5.77:1, 11.27 → 11.28:1, 12.80 → 12.76:1, 12.87 → 12.78:1, 13.04 → 13.05:1, 19.07 → 19.03:1.

Initial draft (decisions selection-control-colors, checked-wins-over-hover, sizes, label-and-description). Native checkbox in a wrapper with a label element and an optional description; states default, hover, focus-visible, checked, indeterminate, invalid, disabled; sizes small and medium. Contrast on the default surface, light / dark: label 19.07 / 11.27, description 12.87 / 8.80, unchecked border 12.87 / 8.80, checked fill 5.79 / 12.80, mark on fill 5.74 / 13.04, error border 6.12 / 3.82, focus ring 5.79 / 12.80.
